checksScope: 393 full-suite tests passed. Renderer-only changes additionally passed 216 shoe-material, 183 sole-transition and 54 cloth-mesh comparisons, plus eight desktop and eight mobile full-scene comparisons. Every comparison was pixel-identical. Physics, contamination, timing and course generation are unchanged.
buildRuntime: Installed Jekyll 4.3.4 / Ruby 3.4.8 with JEKYLL_NO_BUNDLER_REQUIRE; current default Ruby bundle lacks required dependencies.
changes: Sole grain uses fixed Float64 positions and one style/radius per zone instead of recalculating noise, colours and radii for every speck on every repaint.
Denim cubic weights, texture-strip bounds and shoe bend samples are prepared once. Mesh resolution, draw order, antialiasing and flex are unchanged.

Shoe smear offsets are rounded once per physics cell. Water and rinsed residue skip deposit interpolation, relief clearing and smear preparation when no input can reach the existing raised-deposit threshold.
No additional media or canvas textures, reduced resolution, skipped animation or changed physics cadence. The added typed lookup buffers total 12,680 bytes; terrain cache remains capped at 13.18 MiB.

balance.notes: Course geometry, contamination, shoes, race clock and record key are unchanged in this pass; route figures are retained from the previous full verification.

notes: Full-walk wall-clock FPS varied substantially between runs; paired rendering is the stronger comparison. Do not interpret local timings as a universal device guarantee.
Dense-mud shoe painting improved about 31% at the median; overall paired district rendering improved about 3.4%.
Additional footprint-bound and glint lookup arrays total about 4.4 KiB; no new canvas sprites or media.
Public source, live files and Jekyll output match; 23 JavaScript modules pass syntax checks.

The original full-course control varied from 57.1 to 43.3 FPS; optimized runs before the final startup fix ranged from 39.2 to 37.8 FPS. These wall-clock samples are not evidence of a guaranteed frame-rate gain.

The tall-screen prefetch fixture previously moved 740 units per prepared 768-unit tile and eventually stopped short of its next tile. It now advances exactly one tile; the previous timeout was a harness error, not an in-game dead end.
The corrected starved-idle phone test completed in 7.623 seconds versus 21.6435 seconds for the original, about 2.84× faster, with the same 13.18 MiB tile cache.

Final implementation immediately auto-started a complete 100 m walk: 59.9 FPS, 1.52 ms mean game-frame CPU, 3.4 ms p95, no visible tile misses, and 6.8 ms longest prefetch task. No intro-screen idle warm-up was provided; idleFps is null for that reason. Startup longest paint slice was 24.5 ms; the game stays on its intro until opening preparation completes.

startup.method: Four alternating before/after renderer and opening-terrain preparations in one browser, same canvas and seed; medians below exclude the first cold round. Local measurements, not a cross-device guarantee.

notes: Full-route test starts immediately after preparation and uses isolated record storage. The private fixture had a syntax error during its first launch; its builder was fixed and checked before the successful run. No production runtime error was observed.

Native canvas operations remain atomic: setup and rare background operations can exceed the nominal task budget. Full-route maximum frame interval was 34.2 ms; do not claim a universally locked 60 fps.
Denim cached geometry is bounded by seven hem bands and 84 retained splashes per leg; weak maps release old marks and walks. No new media assets or visual simplification.

Paired Node medians alternate implementations for six measured rounds after warmup. Raster work fell 58.6%; prior isolated runs measured 54.8–56.5%. Surface and walk timings vary, so no physics speedup is claimed.

The full route averaged 1.24 ms CPU with 2.6 ms p95, but observed 53.4 fps, two CPU frames over 16.7 ms and a 166.9 ms maximum frame interval. Do not present this as a locked 60 fps full-route result.

Subsequent 12-second wet stress scenes averaged 60 fps at both 1000x760 and 390x844, with CPU p95 5.2 and 4.9 ms. Each had two slow startup frames while building unprimed terrain; reported steady statistics exclude the first 1.5 seconds. The ordinary game primes terrain before enabling start.
Browser cadence without game work was 59.97 fps. The earlier instrumented phase profile is diagnostic only, not a controlled before/after FPS comparison.
No increased canvas sprite budget, new media assets, or per-frame terrain work. Submersion preparation and column tables are temporary work for a newly visible footprint.
Benchmarks are scoped, not a claim of 10x whole-game speed or universal 60 fps. Final paired Node medians: aiming 162.1x faster; full-walk physics CPU 22.6% lower; stationary wet contact 4.6% lower.
Final paired five-district rendering CPU fell 9.7%; dense shoe raster CPU fell 9.5%. Alternate before/after order, six measured Node rounds and 120 measured frames per district.
Full 100 m browser replay averaged 59.9 fps and 1.03 ms CPU (2.1 ms p95), with one slow CPU frame and a 66.7 ms maximum frame interval. Terrain cache stayed at 13.18 MiB with zero visible misses.

Full suite ran after all physics changes. The subsequent separable shader refinement was checked with all 216 material/side/wetness pixel cases and full-scene comparisons. The final version also passed syntax and Jekyll build checks.
Raw profiling, builds and private QA pages are temporary. Existing historical performance records below remain attributed to their original versions.

Timings compare v134 and v135 in alternating order on the same page. Five districts each have 60 warmup frames and 120 measured frames; shoe workloads have three warmup rounds and twenty measured rounds of eight paints.

Both full 100 m routes completed under heavy host CPU contention: v135 at 27.6 FPS and the unchanged v134 control at 15 FPS. These sequential, variably loaded runs are functional checks, not a speedup comparison. Use the paired alternating-frame benchmark for relative rendering costs; do not claim universal 60 FPS.
The full suite passed in 138985 ms. Final shoe, sole, mesh and scene comparisons completed after all renderer edits. The production model has only a cache-key change.
